text:
incident-bot: Pager: High GPU queue growth detected in asia-west1. Autoscaler failing to provision new GPU nodes -> GCP_QUOTA_EXCEEDED. Affected pools: gpu-rt-64, gpu-rt-32. Severity: P1.

matt: ack — oncall here, grabbing logs and perf metrics.

sara: joining. seeing queue_length spike on gpu-rt-64, pending pods in Pending/ContainerCreating with event: 'quota exceeded'.

jen_ops: I'm on the cloud console, quota API shows GPUs: 0 available, request returns 403 Quota has been exceeded for project redwood-prod-asia-west1. Opening support case now.

prod-bot: Deployments paused in asia-west1: rolling deployments auto-suspended due to failed scale attempts.

sandeep: logs from autoscaler: "failed to create instance: compute.googleapis.com/quotaExceeded: requested 4, available 0". Batching backlog is growing; KV cache fills causing longer generation tail latencies.

matt: customer impact: 5m window -> 8% increase in 5xx, median latency up 200ms, p99 > 10s for realtime model. CS reports multiple timed-out requests for orgs with reserved capacity.

customer-success: Confirmed — 3 enterprise accounts have reported timeouts and elevated error rates. We have one ongoing support ticket from AcmeCorp complaining about dropped inference jobs.

matt: immediate mitigations: 1) reduce per-request concurrency on realtime routes for asia-west1 to 1, 2) enable model fallback to cpu-small for non-enterprise-only routes, 3) pause non-critical warm pool fills.

sara: started routing adjustment: sending new non-critical realtime requests to us-central1 amber pool via routing policy. Note: cross-region routing limited by DRY_RUN capacity flags; some requests still attempt asia-west1 first.

jen_ops: filed GCP case CASE-2026-8421, requested quota bump and expedited review. Ticket link: https://console.cloud.google.com/support/cases/CASE-2026-8421 (internal). Also contacting TAM.

sandeep: temporary resource reclamation steps underway: scaling down large-batch workers and job-schedulers in asia-west1 to free GPU slots. Running:

```
kubectl --context=asia-west1 -n inference scale deployment gpu-batcher --replicas=0
kubectl --context=asia-west1 -n inference scale deployment gpu-worker --replicas=1
```

matt: enabling autoscaler fallbacks: force-routing to smaller-quantized model variants (q4_0) for best-effort traffic. Will update routing policy in 2m.

oncall-sre: I'm taking lead for the incident. matt, handoff to me for post-mitigation runbook steps and customer comms. I'll coordinate with CS to prioritize impacted customers.

prod-bot: Canary rollback disabled for safety until quotas stable.

sara: added temporary circuit-breaker on realtime route: reject requests exceeding queue depth > 20 with 429 to avoid cascading failures.

matt: updating incident channel with live metrics snapshot. Queue length (gpu-rt-64): 420 -> 210 after scale-down measures. Pending pods: 86 -> 12. Error rate trending down but still elevated.

customer-success: Noted. We will send a short customer-facing update: "We are aware of elevated errors in APAC (asia-west1) due to cloud GPU quota limits; mitigation in progress, routing to alternate regions for most traffic. ETA ~30-60m."

jen_ops: contacting infra procurement to check reserved capacity options and submit quota increase request template (project-level limits vs account-level).

sandeep: long-term note: need better cross-region warm pool capacity and pre-approved quota increases for asia regions with predictable demand. Adding to roadmap.

matt: next steps: 1) monitor GCP support response, 2) keep routing to us-central1 for best-effort, 3) restore warm pools gradually once quota confirmed. Will update every 10m or on significant change.

oncall-sre: handoff acknowledged. If GCP case delayed > 45m, prepare plan B: customer migration to dedicated pools in us-central1 or enable temporary rate-limits per-tenant.

incident-bot: Incident noted: created incident INC-2026-3447 and linked runbook. Runbook: https://redwood.runbooks/internal/gpu-quota-incident.

matt: thanks team. posting final short summary when stable.
